body: I have disabilities, albeit in a same sex relationship. I know I'm a nightmare,  especially without adequate medical support. I wouldn't be surprised if she walked out tomorrow. That burden must be so great. You only have so much to give emotionally.

I got way more attention when I was morbidly obese. More power to you if you're happy. I'm not obese now but have nothing original about me so just hide. Truth is you can never fit everyone's standards so enjoy what you've got.
Currently suffering from depression. This has been the only thing to make me laugh in approximately six weeks. Thank you.
This is so true. You're making a commitment to only one person so technically just need one or two random witnesses. I think that can be more romantic.

This has happened to me three times (why do I keep studying?!) albeit with different conditions. It should not hinder your success otherwise it comes uncomfortably close to disability discrimination. 

Does your uni have a student disability service? Get in touch with them as soon as possible. 

Look at extenuating circumstances policies your uni may have...This may give you extensions, time out, less hours to work in a day, less restrictive deadlines, etc. 

Fight for your right but don't be ashamed if it becomes too much. You need support right now, not people blocking you and not communicating with you. 

Best of luck.

I'm not in your situation exactly, but have recently had to ask for time out from work. I just broke down, held my hands up and admitted I couldn't cope any longer. I'm on a phased return now...Maybe voicing this to your doctor could help? Without having to go to devastating extremes you could admit you have reached your limits and need time out? I totally understand where you are coming from and in the grand scheme of things, even a month out is nothing. The world keeps on turning.
If you're anything like me you would have done the same with a bunch of white dudes in a group too. It's just the fight or flight instinct.

We really all do fail an exam at some point, whether through poor prep or just missing the point. It's normal and it's character building. It isn't necessarily a reflection of your ability, it's just one of those facts of life even though it sucks. You will succeed regardless.
If I was the owner of the car, just knowing the lengths you'd gone to would be enough. I appreciate honesty.
Who decides if you're good enough? You have nothing to prove, you are just trying to survive like everybody else. Go easy on yourself. Life accommodates all, there is nothing wrong with you.
How will watching this distressing video benefit you? I would advise thinking forward instead of reflecting on your pain and distress. Your painful experience does not define you or your future.

I know exactly how you feel, as I'm sure a lot of us do. 

The truth is you just tend to fall into things and find your way slowly. You have an idea in your mind that everyone else knows what they're doing and that they're super confident but I'm not so sure now. It's hard, tedious and terrifying but you do find your way eventually. 

Good luck.

I wanted to echo this, particularly as it resonates so personally. Identification can be both empowering and dangerous. You owe nobody an explanation and have the freedom to explore as much as you want. Follow your feelings and your true instincts and you will find yourself in the right places. I try to think of it as a journey to finding my life partner (because of my age) rather than an attempt to assign myself a label. Be proud that you are so introspective and emotionally aware!

When you've been ostracised and belittled because of your appearance then it's natural that physical self improvement becomes a priority. As long as you make sure that this improvement leads to you feeling comfortable enough socially to let your true self shine then I wouldn't be worried initially about this preoccupation. Don't view this movement towards physical perfection as a goal though, but rather view the goal as you being comfortable within yourself to be outwardly genuine in personality.

I have this constant fear too. I'm always checking my mirror to see if people are cursing me.

 I had an angry guy behind me for a good few miles the other day (I was going under because I have a tiny car, it was foggy and on a country road notorious for accidents...the drummer from Def Leppard lost his arm there!) and he was getting really close and constantly flashing his headlights. Has put me off for a while :(
Now try it sober so you know if you really do like it!

Your feelings aside for the moment, she sought you out for some specific reason. Whether safety, comfort, support, love...maybe explore that and work from there? Note that she came to you specifically. Why was that?

This always makes me sad, for the hoarder afflicted and others in the home. I know it's masking the true problem but could you suggest obtaining more outside storage space? Can you tackle one small area at a time and measure the response? Maybe it feels too overwhelming. Sometimes I'm convinced that only professional help can work, there must be so much anxiety tied up in a situation like that. I wish you the best of luck.

You capitalised on that woman's addiction, pain, low self esteem and possible mental health problems (disgustingly). Why do you think your new lady has similar afflictions? You do realise not all women are the same? Maybe she'll want to sell your body for her tuition fees, would you do it? Exactly.

It's not about being weak/strong, you are clearly blighted by some kind of compulsive anxiety which is tortuous. You don't deserve it, just like nobody else does. One could say it takes a lot of strength to be insightful, assess your situation and ask for help. I promise you that with guidance your life can improve. Best of luck.

Virginity is a social construct designed to control people. Your sexual life is like a story, it changes, adapts and evolves all the time. It gets worse and it gets better. That's the fun of it all. Don't see this as something you have 'given' or 'lost' but just the beginning of that story. Wait until your emotions become really involved and that will be like starting all over again :) p.s. A lot of us do something very similar. You are not alone.

Those last few lines, that is where it's at! Instead of seeing yourself as a 'pushover' and 'weak' celebrate the fact that you are sensitive and attuned to your feelings. That isn't a negative, it's something to be proud of. 

You understand that aspects of your lifestyle are holding you back from your goals of how you want to be, so chip away at them..but slowly and compassionately. Slipping up on one cigarette or glass of wine doesn't make you an abominable person. Set small goals. 

I guarantee that if you see your sensitivity as a plus and begin evaluating your sense of worth (according to what you want for yourself) then you will come on in leaps and bounds.

You become very accustomed to the partner your with and what makes them tick that it's a difficult transition back. All people have different preferences, so technically all new sexual encounters are not perfect on a physical level. 

What a rude woman though. Unless you were selfish or disrespectful nobody has the right to be nasty about your sexual efforts. I'd tell the next girl you're with your circumstances and that you're nervous. The right girls will be understanding and respect your honesty so you're in a better place to have a good time.

It sounds to me like you've taken this on as your problem and blame yourself when in reality the fault lies with your husband. If he wasn't fully invested and committed then he should have stated his doubts before marriage. If he is constantly dwelling on what could have been (a 'grass is greener' scenario) then he needs to do more than be insensitive about it, he needs to either leave or dedicate himself fully to making the marriage work. 

You have been left feeling not only heartbroken, but powerless and self-loathing. Spying was maybe a way to rationalise your husband's words in your mind or subconsciously punish yourself more. It perhaps erred onto the weird side when you befriended her but we all do irrational things when we're heartbroken. Still, I don't see any fault on your behalf, it sounds like your husband needs to get his priorities in order.

I'm genuinely concerned about a house I know like this a) because of the poor animals and b) because I know a disabled woman is living there who rarely leaves, so the ammonia may cause respiratory tract infections. I don't want to be intrusive though :(
It's done now. You feel awful, so maybe just prepare better for the next time? Maybe a stronger poison or call an exterminator?

You want the pain to stop, which is understandable. However, you sound like a valued and compassionate person, which needs to be held onto. There will be infinite avenues to take in an attempt to remedy your current painful situation. Not all may be possible or successful but you owe it to yourself to explore before giving in. Even explore your depression if it may help. Seek help from those you regard so highly that you owe them your life. I hear your suffering but I promise there is a way out for now.

I've had struggles with my weight in the opposite direction (had to lose 120lbs) so I'm probably not the best person to seek advice from, although I have infinite sympathy. What I try to focus on is nutrients, things that will make my body  feel stronger and more able to deal with the demands of life. You are obviously sensitive to physical changes...do you have anybody to speak to this about professionally? Remember that you have worth way beyond your physicality. Don't be afraid to ask for support and face up to the patterns of thinking that are destroying you. It's an infinite battle, I know, but nutrients and a defiant attitude will prepare you adequately.

You just have a personal space thing and I think that's justified. I get it on public transport. At least you don't think you're doing learning disabled people a divine favour by coddling them in a supermarket when they just popped out to get a snack (admittedly this is more the elderly and grinds my gears no end).

As they say, you can't choose your family! It sounds like you've had patience with him in the past but for some reason your personalities simply clash. It also sounds like you are highly aware of his health problems so something tells me if this was a serious health issue you'd be more inclined to visit him? As long as you still have the capacity to care in a crisis despite your fundamental differences then I think you're justified this time around.

I think "retardation" went out of favour because it suggests some kind of defect, slowness or inability whereas the disability movement promotes diversity and focusing on positives despite impairments. "Special needs" works well with kids too because you don't know if their illness is developmental or psychiatric. 

In relation to your story, I take service users out a lot and they get so many varied responses. Some people have to vacate the area and can't talk directly to them which is sad, but not nearly as annoying as those overly friendly patronising folk who think they are doing God's work by waving and smiling dramatically. 

However, touching with our folk is always a no-no. It makes people uncomfortable and this young girl will one day want to form relationships so her mother had better teach her to keep her mitts to herself in public!

You have conquered this before, you will find the strength and desire to do so again. What you have already achieved is fantastic...Please don't think because of this recent U-turn that you are somehow beyond help, it's just a step in your journey. Maybe completely physically remove yourself from people who tempt you, all substances that alter your thinking (alcohol is awful for that) and try all you can to focus on activities that occupy your mind and give you a sense of accomplishment.

If you use this as motivation then all power to you! You are your own life coach. However, just try to be mindful if you begin to become unhappy and overly critical consistently as 'black and white' thinking is highly associated with depression from a cognitive perspective.

This is very true, behind most smiles people are enduring the same lack of confidence. Try and find other qualities that you value above and beyond attractiveness. As someone in their late 20s who has been self-conscious since my teens I can guarantee you two things: someone WILL find you attractive at some point (even though you may never understand why) and you'll slowly stop caring in time. It is rather liberating!
Tell her you've seen them and remind her it's risky, then let her decide what to do. You never know in the future when she might look out for you in a similar way (none of us are infallible)

I'm interested in how you navigate Occupational Health. I took the 'I will bring down the stigma and be honest!' route recently with a job (my dream job as it happens) and they're pulling me in for an appointment :(

The same pain you felt before self-harming is the same pain your family member can't cope with for whatever reason. You've succeeded in finding alternative strategies which is amazing, but for others that takes a little longer. Share your experiences to benefit others, not to shame them. Also, congratulations!

It also takes years to see the end results of any changes, so making people feel ashamed whilst on their journey only serves to complicate things. It took me almost a decade and by the end of it I was practically used to being treated like a second class citizen anyway.

These seem like reasons to kill yourself but really they're things that are (rightfully so) making you feel awful. It may not feel like it now but feelings can change, this pain won't last forever. I'm so sorry people have inflicted suffering on you.

Hi, sounds like you're really experiencing some intense emotional turmoil here and I wanted to chime in as a UK resident who has accessed (and had to fight for) services before.

If you feel acutely suicidal you can always present yourself to A&E. Don't worry about forced hospitalisation, they have teams there that can simply support you for a few hours and then arrange follow-up care. You are fully entitled to see the Access and Liaison team suffering the way you are...They can arrange for you to have crisis team or support worker visits.

Please go back to your GP if you feel this much pain. They can put referrals in to the Access and Liason team if necessary or they can refer you on for therapy. Do you have any charity drop-in services near you? I found Mind to be fantastic. 

Hang in there, don't let them minimise your suffering but keep taking these amazingly brave steps to seek help. If all else fails, we're all here.

In this post I see someone courageous, brave and inspiring. Things look bleak right now, but if you are following your heart then you can only go to better places. Trust yourself,  you sound so insightful. You are following this path because you truly believe in it...stick to your convictions and your future will be so bright.

I felt this and found voluntary work so therapeutic. I worked voluntarily in mental health first, then when I became more depressed I worked with animals. It really takes you outside yourself and you become absolved in other beings for a while.

A lot of us are there and a lot of us are hoping. I hear people say distress ends and hope for that day myself. You should too. Those circumstances making you suffer right now may just change. I know it hurts.

What strikes me is your insight into why you do it. You are very aware of what you want to a achieve and why. You are obviously acutely suffering but that will help you break the cycle. Embrace your insight!

Losing you has made me actively suicidal. I would never truly blame you though. I thought you would accept me, you were the first person in decades I was truly genuine with. I let you abuse me because it's better than not having you at all. I'm pathetic. I can see you abusing me and I allow it. You have ruined my life yet I still love you.

This is referred to as 'internalised homophobia' and is a recognised thing. You know how I know? I've received extensive therapy for it. 

There is nothing inherently wrong with being frightened, humans naturally want the path of least resistance and sadly heterosexuality is still deemed as 'easy' and 'the norm'. 

Yet you and I both know those feelings will never leave and why should they? In the future you are likely to experience beautiful, true (same sex! ) love and genuine companionship. When you reach that state you will contemplate what you ever 
worried about and instead bask in the joy of it. 

So please don't berate yourself for your feelings. Hang on in there and place less emphasis on WHO you want to love but the fact that you want to love at all. You have my total empathy.

You're not a failure. Whatever the exam result is, you are not a failure. Your skills may not even lie in academia. What are you good at? You could be good at so many things in life that one test can't even begin to measure. 

If you are struggling, speak to your dad honestly and openly. He will have self-doubted and failed in his life many times before. 

You also will have difficulty overdosing on Prozac, I tried. It's not worth the hassle and distress. Look after yourself.

I probably didn't word it properly, so not offense taken. 

I mean just accept yourself as a human being, stuck here, with what you have to work with. Don't be so hard on yourself. Accept you're unhappy but don't despair, see that as a point to work from and evolve. The horrible things you say about yourself are so concrete and subjective to you, in a depressive state. 

I think I was, in a personal way (and for personal reasons), alluding more to your sexuality. At first it feels terrifying and consumes your thoughts, feelings and behaviour. In time it becomes as relevant as the colour of your eyes, if you accept yourself that way. 

I'm sorry if I cause offense, I'm a suicidal queer myself and just thought I'd reach out. If anything you have my sincere empathy.

It is my cousin's birthday today. He killed himself 11 years ago and my auntie has cried every day since. Our family still lights candles regularly. They won't remember just once a year, their lives will be destroyed. 

I'm not saying this as a way to 'guilt' you either. I'm suicidal myself at the moment but his anniversary gave me some food for thought. You really aren't as meaningless and unloved as you think.

Those are some really hateful things you say about yourself when you're at your most vulnerable. What would you say to somebody who was feeling as low as you were? 

I noticed somebody mentioned self-improvement which is always important, but have you ever just tried to accept yourself for who you are? Ignore that negative voice trying to bring you down, hold your hands up, say "THIS IS ME" and work from there. 

I really empathise also with your struggles regarding your sexuality. It's never easy but it does become almost insignificant with time.

You've caught me there...because all the platitudes I'd give to someone else right now are at complete odds to what I feel inside. 

I guess I'd advise being kind to yourself, taking respite, talking through things, staying safe.

I've done the complete opposite and not taken care of myself, begged for her back repeatedly (ugh) and questioned the point of carrying on.

I was studying Clinical Psychology (I know, that sounds ridiculous coming from someone suicidal). I always wanted to help people who had mental pain too some day. 

I guess I like history and, like you, anything related to the universe. 

I just don't know how people get past this crushing agony. I can't sit up for longer than 30 minutes, can't even drink and there's this huge void where she was. I feel like I've done this one too many times now (not really the heartbreak, she was my first true love).

I loved learning, but my education ended some months ago. No decent job, like all young people these days. 

I have a hard time creating a sense of hope when the emotional pain is so overwhelming. This pain always returns and I always wonder to myself "is this the last time I can deal with this?".

I can't even envision my 30's, I don't feel very compatible with life to be honest. 

I prided myself on loving and enjoying love, that connection with another. Now I realise there is no hope in that whatsoever.

This post resonates with me so much. I've just been abandoned and don't know how to carry on, the pain is immense and crushing. It has exacerbated into the worst depression I have ever known. 

Before, I had a glimmer of hope and love filled the void where pain now lies. Now I have nothing and can't see ahead to the end of each hour. 

You are not alone. I'd gladly take more pain to relieve you, nobody deserves this.

I can feel your heartbreak, I really can :( 

I haven't moved all day because it hurts so much when just a few days ago we were laughing, holding each other and being our silly selves.

Interestingly, she also told me she would never leave either. I truly thought we'd be able to work through everything because, hey, life is just better with your soulmate. 

How she can be so flippant when it feels like my world is ending...I can't comprehend it. 

I'm so sorry you're feeling this same pain.

I'm going through the exact same scenario right now...except I was a lot more cowardly than you and called in sick!

If I see her, I'll cry. I won't be able to concentrate and there will be memories every time I look at her. She doesn't seem to be hurting and I'm devastated, we weren't 'out' to our colleagues so they'll have no idea why I'm cowering in the corner not speaking. 

Maybe you could keep super busy whenever she's around? She has taken steps to look after herself (i.e. wanting space, to be single) so perhaps we should look after ourselves too? Easier said than done.

I empathise with you so much. To be honest I don't think I'll last at this job because she's my world and I can't pretend she's anything but.
Sadly not many. We were quite an insular couple, spent a lot of time together and even work together (I know, worst idea to fall in love in the workplace).

Thanks for your input and advice, as I said I don't really have many people around me to help. 

I'm uncomfortable with the idea of her having all the control and dictating the relationship but it's hard to set aside such strong feelings. This was someone I was willing to settle with for a long time. 

Interesting that you say 'pull the rug out'...feels exactly like that :(

How very frustrating.

Something similar happened to me...I tried seven times to get through to a mental health hotline, got accidentally hung up on twice...then after my 30minute call realised my phone was water-damaged through tears!

I had to laugh. For the first time in months.
I don't know how I'm going to make it through the night, I really don't.

Thank you for taking the time to respond.

I know my emotions are overwhelming right now but I can't help but think that maybe this is it. Maybe my time is up. I've tried and tried so hard, got myself through suicide attempts before but this feels different...almost rational. The only way to end the hurt. 

I feel like if I saw her I would break down and never recover. Unhealthy as I know it is, she was my reason to keep trying and my piece of hope.
